description:
On develop f822f0f84 this fails on interp ('backend type test cannot read lane-form ShapeId(..)') and on run ('native type test cannot read lane-form'):

  def kind(n :: integer), do: {:int, n}
  def kind(f :: ((integer) -> integer)), do: {:fn, f.(10)}
  def pick(flag, a, b) do
    case flag do
      true -> a
      _ -> b
    end
  end
  def main() do
    n = Process.heap_alloc_stats()[:allocs]
    flag = n < n + 1
    dbg(kind(pick(flag, fn (x) -> x + 1 end, 5)))
  end

Elixir prints {:fn, 11}.

Mechanism (measured with a local print): the value reaches kind's integer test as ShapeDescr::Callable with zero lanes. Transport gives it the exact direct-callable layout (layout_from_demand -> callable_layout_from_demand -> exact_direct_callable_layout) because its runtime demand is callable and names one target, though its type is closure | int. A direct callable has no room for the integer. Only a join of DISTINCT callable producers is marked escaped (runtime_demand.rs delivered_join_has_distinct_callable_producers, whose filter_map drops non-callable and parameter sources). Fixture 00632 passes on develop only because its three callers blend three lambdas into one return (the fz-lr6 bug), which trips that rule.

Refuted placement: gating the exact layout on a pure-callable type gets past the type test and then fails at the apply seam ('reached function N through the apply seam, which publishes no construction wrapper'). Boxing is a runtime-demand fact (CallableDemand::escape) read by both the layout and the wrapper publication, so the decision belongs there, once.

Acceptance:
- new oracle fixture with the program above (and a two-caller variant) passes on interp, run and build;
- 00632 still passes, and passes with fz-lr6's change;
- one rule in runtime demand, stated in pipeline.md: a callable value whose type admits anything but that callable is first-class;
- pin moves attributed; rises authorized.
title: A value that may be a callable or something else travels boxed, so a type test and a call can both read it
